extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, USPTO OED staff, and legal professionals involved in practitioner discipline
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluation and approval of an Affidavit of Resignation filed under 37 C.F.R. § 11.27, and the resulting exclusion on consent from practice before the USPTO; includes related notice, publication, and reinstatement consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit of Resignation (37 C.F.R. § 11.27) — voluntariness and informed consent
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent's consent is freely and voluntarily rendered, and he is not being subjected to coercion or duress; respondent acknowledges awareness of the investigation and the legal/factual consequences of consenting to exclusion under 37 C.F.R. § 11.27.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The affidavit must show the practitioner (1) freely and voluntarily consents, (2) is aware an OED investigation was opened and the allegations under investigation, and (3) fully understands the legal and factual consequences of consenting to exclusion, including the regulatory provisions cited (e.g., 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.5(b), 11.27, 11.58, 11.59, and 11.60). The Director approved the affidavit because it complied with § 11.27(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit content — acknowledgment of investigated facts
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent acknowledges factual findings developed in the investigation (e.g., role at firm, representation of particular client, sending fraudulent bills between approximately November 2006 and June 2014, client payments, and guilty plea to eight counts of mail fraud).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The affidavit may include admissions or acknowledgments of factual circumstances underlying the OED investigation; such acknowledgments are relied upon by the OED Director and may be conclusively presumed for reinstatement purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admission of awareness of OED's opinion of rule violations
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is aware that the OED Director is of the opinion that he violated specified provisions of the USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility and/or the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The affidavit should indicate the respondent's awareness of the OED Director's opinion identifying particular disciplinary provisions believed violated (see specific cited provisions). The respondent need not admit the violations but acknowledges the OED's opinion and consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility violations cited (37 C.F.R. § 10.23 variants)
rubrics_metrics.description: OED alleges violations of: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(a) (A practitioner shall not engage in disreputable or gross misconduct); 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(3) (A practitioner shall not engage in illegal conduct involving moral turpitude); and 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(4) (A practitioner shall not engage in conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the substantive standards (applicable to conduct prior to May 3, 2013) the OED may rely on when forming an opinion about a practitioner's misconduct. The affidavit may acknowledge that the OED holds the opinion that these provisions were violated.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct violations cited (37 C.F.R. § 11.804 variants)
rubrics_metrics.description: OED alleges violations of: 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(b) (It is professional misconduct for a practitioner to commit a criminal act that reflects adversely on the practitioner's honesty, trustworthiness or fitness); 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(c) (It is professional misconduct to engage in conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation); and 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(i) (It is professional misconduct to engage in other conduct that adversely reflects on the practitioner's fitness to practice before the USPTO).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the Rules of Professional Conduct (applying to conduct on or after May 3, 2013) that OED may allege a practitioner violated; the affidavit may reflect awareness of such alleged rule violations even if the practitioner does not admit them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director's authority to approve exclusion on consent (statutory and regulatory basis)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director has authority to approve an Affidavit of Resignation and to exclude a practitioner on consent from practice before the USPTO pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.27.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approval depends on the affidavit's compliance with regulatory requirements (e.g., § 11.27(a)); the Director acts under the cited statutory/regulatory framework to enter the Final Order excluding the practitioner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of exclusion on consent — scope and commencement
rubrics_metrics.description: When approved, the respondent is excluded on consent from practice before the Office in patent, trademark, and other non-patent matters commencing on the date of the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order specifies the scope (patent, trademark, other non-patent matters) and effective date of the exclusion; the practitioner must cease practice before the Office accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and notice requirements following exclusion on consent
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall electronically publish the Final Order at the OED Reading Room and publish a notice in the Official Gazette containing specified information about the exclusion and the OED's opinion of rule violations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public notice includes practitioner name, registration number, statement that affidavit was accepted and exclusion ordered, summary of underlying facts (e.g., fraudulent billing and criminal plea), the specific regulatory provisions the OED believes were violated, and the legal authority for the action (35 U.S.C. and 37 C.F.R. citations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement consequence — conclusory presumption under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent acknowledges that if and when he applies for reinstatement under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60, the OED Director will conclusively presume, for the purpose of determining the application for reinstatement, that (a) the facts set forth in the affidavit and investigation are true, and (b) he could not have successfully defended against the allegations embodied in the OED Director's opinion that he violated the cited disciplinary provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This presumption is a critical reinstatement standard a practitioner consents to accept when submitting an affidavit under § 11.27; it affects the burden and evaluation in any future § 11.60 reinstatement proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligations to comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 and § 11.60
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 (duties upon suspension or exclusion) and with 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 upon any request for reinstatement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order expressly requires compliance with the cited provisions: § 11.58 governs practitioner duties following suspension or exclusion (e.g., notice to clients, transfer of files) and § 11.60 sets forth the reinstatement procedures and requirements the respondent must follow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporal applicability of disciplinary regimes
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility (37 C.F.R. § 10.20 et seq.) applies to conduct prior to May 3, 2013; the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct (37 C.F.R. § 11.101 et seq.) apply to conduct on or after May 3, 2013.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing alleged misconduct spanning dates before and after May 3, 2013, OED and the practitioner must reference the appropriate disciplinary regime for the conduct's date(s).
